title: How do we build a bigger house with every side seven centimetres?
description: The house is built again with every border line seven centimetres, using the same steps as before. The top point is found from two compass arcs of seven centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same order of drawing works for any size, and only the compass opening changes. Watch for students who keep the old opening of five centimetres.

video_script.why: A learner repeats the house construction with a new size, changing the length of the sides and the compass opening to seven centimetres.
video_script.substitution: the house with the base DE of seven centimetres, the walls DB and EC, the roof sides AB and AC, and the arc from B to C, all seven centimetres
video_script.anchor: a bigger house with the base DE, the walls DB and EC, the roof meeting at A, and the arc from B to C, every line 7 cm
video_script.payoff_line: The bigger house is ready, with every border line seven centimetres long.

final_answer.value: a house with DE = DB = EC = AB = AC = 7 cm, apex A 7 cm from B and from C, and an arc from B to C with centre A and radius 7 cm
final_answer.spoken: the bigger house is ready, with every border line seven centimetres long

maths_rules: the base DE is 7 cm, and the walls DB and EC are perpendicular to DE and 7 cm each
the door can be 2 cm wide and 3 cm tall on the base
A is 7 cm from B and 7 cm from C, so it is where an arc from B meets an arc from C
the arc from B to C is drawn with centre A and radius 7 cm
video_script.design: The first house is shown faintly beside the new one. The compass opening changes from five to seven centimetres, and every other step repeats.
